item.title: Large expansion of Meals on Wheels Tralee premises planning for 2026
item.description: Meals on Wheels Tralee and Killarney is planning a large expansion of its Tralee premises in 2026. The service extended into the Killarney area in February 2025. Works are currently underway to expand its range of services in Tralee, including a community café. Advertisement The director of Meals on Wheels Tralee and Killarney, Paddy Kevane, says an extension will be open shortly. Those interested in finding out more about the charity’s work may visit MealsOnWheelsTralee.ie.

item.title: Councillor says delays to grants for maintaining graveyards should not happen again
item.description: A north Kerry councillor has called for delays to grants for the maintenance of graveyards not to happen again. Councillor Jimmy Moloney claimed that this year’s grants only began to be paid out in the week before the Listowel Municipal District (MD) November meeting. He said this was unsatisfactory, adding that the community groups responsible for the maintenance of burial grounds do most of their work in the summer, when the weather is fine. item.description: St Brendans Tralee can this coming Saturday become All-Ireland champions. The final of the U18 Men’s National Cup sees them go head to head with Dublin Lions, from 2.30 at the National Arena in Dublin. Brendan's coach Gareth Moore reflects on the campaign to date Advertisement

item.title: Geaney believes All Ireland final will be special and emotional
item.description: Dingle's Paul Geaney believes their AIB All Ireland Senior Club Football Championship final will be special and emotional. Following comeback victories against St.Finbarrs and Ballyboden, this Sunday sees the Kerry and Munster champions seek to complete the season with a national title. They'll take on St.Brigids from Roscommon at 3.40 in Croke Park. Advertisement Geaney doesn't think it'll be different for those who haven't played at the venue before

item.title: Celtic manager trying to secure signings
item.description: Martin O'Neill has told Celtic fans the club are "really trying" to secure further January signings. Centre-back Stephen Welsh has been recalled from his loan spell at Motherwell, while Mexico defender Julian Araujo arrived on loan from Bournemouth. O'Neill began his second spell this season as interim boss with a 4-nil win over Dundee United at the weekend and is looking to add to his squad. Advertisement

item.title: Mixed injury news for Munster; Kleyn to depart province
item.description: There is mixed news on the injury front for Munster ahead of their Champions Cup match against Castres on Saturday. Wing Calvin Nash is out with a head and shoulder injury while Paddy Patterson has also been ruled out with a head knock. Craig Casey could still be available despite suffering a shoulder injury in the defeat to Toulon. item.title: HSE holds free walk-in 'flu vaccine clinics for children in Kerry
item.description: Kerry parents are being encouraged to bring their children to the HSE's free walk-in clinics, to get them vaccinated against the 'flu. The vaccine is administered by nasal spray and is a quick and painless procedure. It provides strong and effective protection for children aged 2–17 years, helping to reduce illness and prevent the spread of flu within households. item.title: Kerry MEP says farmers fears over Mercosur are exaggerated
item.description: A Kerry MEP says Irish farmers fears over Mercosur are exaggerated. Last week a majority of EU member states voted in favour of the deal, which will now go back to MEPs to have their say. Ireland voted against the deal last week - as promised in the Programme for Government. Advertisement Farmers here are concerned about the standard of beef which will be imported from South American countries, if the agreement is approved.
